content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a 4 or 8 part round braid, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Apply finishing wax to the ends of the cords (5 minutes)
Step 2. Measure the final length of the woven section (2 minutes)
Step 3. Select a decorative metal end cap (10 minutes)
Step 4. Prepare the jewelry adhesive (3 minutes)
Step 5. Organize the workspace for the next project (15 minutes)
Step 6. Cut the leather cords into equal lengths (8 minutes)
Step 7. Group the cords into two sets of four (4 minutes)
Step 8. Burnish the edges of the finished braid (12 minutes)
Step 9. Attach a temporary weight to the cord ends (1 minute)
Step 10. Thread the cords through a centering disk (6 minutes)
Step 11. Choose the cord colors from the inventory (20 minutes)
Step 12. Untangle the cord spools (10 minutes)
Step 13. Unroll the required yardage (2 minutes)
Step 14. Begin the over-under weaving pattern (30 minutes)
Step 15. Trim the excess fringe (4 minutes)
Step 16. Secure the starting knot with a rubber band (2 minutes)
Step 17. Inspect the cords for any fraying or defects (5 minutes)
Step 18. Soak the cords in water to increase flexibility (1 hour)
Step 19. Bind the top of the cords with twine (6 minutes)
Step 20. Arrange the cords in a radial pattern (5 minutes)
Step 21. Tighten the tension of the weave (10 minutes)
Step 22. Taper the ends of the cords for easier handling (7 minutes)
Step 23. Light a candle to singe synthetic fiber ends (2 minutes)
Step 24. Label each cord position 1 through 8 (8 minutes)
Step 25. Complete the final round of braiding (25 minutes)
Step 26. Buff the braid with a soft cloth (3 minutes)
Step 27. Cross the left-most strand over the center (1 minute)
Step 28. Adjust the tension on the centering disk (4 minutes)
Step 29. Wipe away excess moisture from the strands (5 minutes)
Step 30. Set the braid aside to dry and settle (4 hours)
Step 31. Clean the braiding surface (10 minutes)
Step 32. Sharpen the cutting shears (15 minutes)
Step 33. Position the cords into the starting slots (5 minutes)
Step 34. Check the braid consistency against a template (9 minutes)
Step 35. Calibrate the tension weight (10 minutes)
Step 36. Double-check the numbering of the strands (2 minutes)
Step 37. Rotate the braiding disk 90 degrees (30 seconds)
Step 38. Prepare a storage bag for the finished braid (1 minute)
Step 39. Mix the two-part epoxy for the clasp (5 minutes)
Step 40. Measure the circumference of the braid (3 minutes)
